proposed_change.summary: The published storefront-buyer-facing checklist (38 checks, context version 3) has no case for any risk this task identified. Propose adding six reusable test conditions once the behaviour is confirmed.
proposed_change.self_declared_gap: The checklist itself already excludes the BOUNDARY dimension with the reason 'Khong co evidence ve gioi han kich thuoc/so luong/do dai/dinh dang trong run nay (vd max ky tu ten ca nhan hoa, gioi han upload ...)'. It names upload limits explicitly as unevidenced. This KCP asks for that exclusion to be revisited now that a task has made the area concrete.

proposed_checks.condition: Two distinct visitors on the same device model/region/browser build must not share an upload quota. No existing check exercises two concurrent private sessions on one device.
proposed_checks.risk: Fallback-ID collision across buyers - the reported bug.

proposed_checks.condition: A genuine repeat visitor is still limited after the fix, including across a page reload inside the same window; the fallback ID must be stable per browser as well as unique per browser.
proposed_checks.risk: Over-correction: an ID regenerated too often silently disables rate limiting. See requirement-analysis RISK-01 and CONF-02.

proposed_checks.condition: Thumbmark fetch resilience: 8s timeout, exactly one retry on network error/5xx, and no retry on 429.
proposed_checks.risk: A retry on 429 would amplify load against the endpoint's own IP-keyed limit.

proposed_checks.condition: localStorage teeinblue_signed_thumbmark lifecycle: written at page load with no expiry, reused on later loads so no second GET fires; cleared or incognito produces a fresh fetch.
proposed_checks.risk: Cache behaviour is easily misread as a bug - comment 51220 warns testers about exactly this.

proposed_checks.condition: AI-effect gating: a plain upload with no AI effect is never rate limited, while an upload using an AI effect is.
proposed_checks.risk: An identity-path fix could accidentally change which uploads are counted.

proposed_change.constraint: These are candidate reusable conditions, not TIB-5460 test cases. Per the contract, any check without a confirmed oracle must be published as NEEDS_CONFIRMATION. Right now none of them has a confirmed oracle - the expected results exist only in Jira comment 51220.
